process: lost wax (report.json draft.process = "Lost wax"; the lost-wax gates apply, the sand gates do not)
summary: Revise at 6.3. Caiman is 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every lost-wax gate is green in report.json and report-draft.json. I also checked finished-metal.stl and casting-pattern.stl independently: 1,438,012 triangles each, every edge shared by exactly 2 faces, 0 degenerate faces, and the minimum radius is 9.3000 mm, so nothing enters the 18.6 mm bore. This is the first Moloch that reads as an animal. With no caption, face-300 is a spiky lizard with four legs, a head, a false-head hump and a whorled tail that shrinks from head to tip. The side view gives the ring a silhouette no other Cataphracta ring or Reptilia tile has. The modelling is what holds it well under 7.5. (1) The four limbs are smooth, even tubes with ball elbows and knees and blob feet. In face.png the front legs read as duck or penguin shapes, not thorned lizard limbs. They also reach 2-3 mm past each side face, which is a snag and a wear problem. (2) The two hemispherical 'hump spine' domes at the nape, each topped by a cone, and the dome beside the snout read as eyes in hero-300 and stones.png. The section says no eyes. (3) The body between the cones is bare polished metal with a sparse scatter of 0.3 mm beads, so the small-scale hide the thorny devil is known for is missing. Hero-300 still leans toward hedgehog or urchin. (4) The 'sand ripples' band hide is soft and smeared rather than crisp. It shows vertical tile seams in palm.png, side.png and reverse.png, and the lozenge row on the side faces reads as tyre tread. (5) The toes run down to 0.11 mm sections over 10.6 mm² and are waved through as 'cleaned up with a graver'. A graver cannot restore metal that never filled. All five can be fixed in the two rounds left.
strengths: Reads as an animal at 300 px with no caption. Face-300 shows head, four splayed legs, a thorned body and a tapering tail: a spiky lizard, and most viewers would say thorny devil.

The silhouette belongs to this ring alone. In side.png a figure lies along the crown and its whorled tail wraps down the shoulder to about -60 deg. Nothing on the Reptilia sheet or elsewhere in Cataphracta looks like it.

The thorns grade clearly by kind (brow horns 4, hump spines 2, major 22, minor 33, tail 31), running big at the nape and small at the tail tip. The thorns are now broad-based cones, not needles, which fixes read-test-1 change 2 in part.
The tail is round, tapers and carries whorled cones. The read-test-1 fishbone read is gone.
The build is clean. Coarse, draft and export builds are all watertight and uncrossed, the made part joins, the field is Castable with a 1.66 mm thinnest wall, and the export is 1.44 M triangles.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: One subject: a thorny devil lying on a sand-ripple band that stands for its habitat. The palm is quiet ripple band and nothing stray sits there. The band's tile seams (punch 5) are a finish fault, not a theme fault.

checklist.item: The hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px, not generic scales or texture
checklist.reason: The animal reads from its outline (legs, head, tail). The hide does not: cones stand on smooth polished skin with only sparse 0.3 mm beads, with none of the devil's knobbed, granular scale field. In hero-300 the legs hide under the cones, and the nape domes read as a pair of eyes over a hedgehog bristle.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines that render crisp, with no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The sculpted part's outlines are crisp. The band hide 'Sand ripples' renders smeared and melted, with vertical seams at its tile boundaries (palm.png near x 500 and x 850; side.png near 10 and 12 o'clock; reverse.png at the top). The side-face lozenge row also reads as a combed tread.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: No stones by design (0 previewed, 0 reported). Not applicable.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The body and head are sculpted, but the limbs are uniform smooth tubes with spherical elbow and knee lumps and blob toes. They read as a toy or cartoon (duck shapes in face.png), not as a lizard's tapering, thorned limbs.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: In bare-vs-finished.png and hero.png the bore-to-side and side-to-crown breaks survive. The ripple relief softens the crown edge somewhat, but the angle still reads.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and from the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: The figure on the crown and the tail wrapping the shoulder are unlike every Reptilia tile. This is the only figure-on-band ring in the collection.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large forms (body, head, tail) and medium forms (cones, horns) are present. The small scale is missing on the body, limbs and head: there are smooth patches over 2 mm across between the cones in face.png. Overall density is below Caiman's hero.

gates.verified: Checked independently on finished-metal.stl: 1,438,012 triangles, 718,998 vertices, 0 edges not shared by exactly 2 faces, 0 degenerate triangles. Euler characteristic -8 (genus 5), so there are 4 handles beyond the band. These are presumably the tunnels under the limbs and tail. Investment fills them, and they are not a gate.

gates.claimed: main.self_crossings 0; made_part_crossings Thorny devil 0; sculpt.self_crossings 0, open_edges 0

Minimum vertex radius in both STLs is 9.3000 mm.

gates.gate: Field verdict Castable with the 0.8 mm fill
gates.claimed: field.verdict Castable, band_verdict Castable, min_section 0.8, thinnest wall 1.658 mm
gates.verified: The verdict is 'Castable', not 'with care'. The notes list ripple undercuts only as two-part information.

gates.gate: land_widths: every section under 0.8 mm removed or named with its bench treatment
gates.claimed: unnamed_under_floor []; toes, hump spines, brow horns, major, minor and tail thorns named
gates.verified: The per-kind under-floor areas sum to 54.63 mm², which matches part_sections.under_floor_mm2 54.63. Every kind has a treatment, so the gate passes as written. However, the toes reach 0.111 mm over 10.6 mm² with the treatment 'claws cleaned up with a graver'. That will short-fill in investment, and a graver removes metal, it cannot add it (punch 2).

gates.verified: Matches; the ring has no stones by design.
true in report.json. The draft build does not run it, as expected.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: all four limbs (front pair at about theta 95-105 deg, rear pair at about theta 130-140 deg in face.png)
punch_list.change: Re-sculpt the limbs from even tubes into lizard limbs. Taper each upper limb from 1.4 mm at the body to 0.9 mm at the wrist. Remove the spherical elbow and knee lumps and replace them with a gentle bend. Add 3-5 cone thorns per limb, 0.4-0.6 mm tall with 0.5-0.7 mm bases, on the upper surface, matching the minor-thorn style. Pull each limb in so it drapes down the side face and lies on it: no part of any limb may extend more than 0.8 mm past the side face in Z (today it is about 2-3 mm).
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png every limb outline stays within band width + 0.8 mm on each side, and no limb has a round joint lump. In hero-300 at least three limbs are visible, and each reads as a thorned lizard leg, not a smooth tube or a duck shape.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: toes on all four feet (land_widths kind 'toes', thinnest 0.111 mm at 104 deg)
punch_list.change: Rebuild each foot as 5 splayed toes, 0.8-1.0 mm long and at least 0.5 mm thick at the root, lying flat on and fused to the band surface. Tips may round to 0.3 mm. Drop the graver treatment.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json land_widths toes thinnest_mm >= 0.45 and under_floor_mm2 <= 2.0. In stones.png and face.png each foot shows 5 distinct toes gripping the band.

punch_list.zone: Nape and head: the two 'hump spines' domes (about theta 95 deg, v near the crest) and the dome beside the snout (left end in stones.png)
punch_list.change: Remove every hemispherical cap-plus-cone. Make the false head one low nuchal knob, about 3 mm across and 1.2-1.5 mm high, whose flanks run continuously into two stout cones with 1.0-1.2 mm bases. Leave no spherical bulge or ring-shaped shadow at the cone roots. Replace the dome beside the snout with a brow horn or smooth it into the head.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 and face-300 nothing reads as a pair of eyes: no round dark-ringed dots at the head or nape. In stones.png the nape shows one knob carrying two cones, with no ball under each cone.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: dorsal body skin and tail top between the cones (theta about 90-170 deg, and the tail from 170 deg to its tip)
punch_list.change: Add the devil's small-scale hide: a close field of rounded tubercles and granules, 0.4-0.7 mm across, 0.15-0.3 mm high, at about 0.9 mm pitch, with a few 0.8-1.0 mm keeled knobs mixed in. Cover all bare skin between the cones on the body, the upper limbs and the head, so that the eye reads large cones, then medium knobs, then fine granules.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png no smooth patch on the body or head is larger than 1.5 mm across. In hero-300 the body reads as knobbed reptile hide under the thorns, not as a hedgehog or urchin. Every relief stays at or above the 0.15 mm detail floor, with no new unnamed entries in land_widths.

punch_list.zone: Band hide 'Sand ripples' (full circumference, crown and shoulders) and the lozenge row on both side faces
punch_list.change: Make the ripple tiling seamless: use one tile around the ring, or a tile count whose ends match exactly. Sharpen it into crisp dune ripples, about 0.25 mm crest height, 1.2-1.5 mm wavelength, asymmetric sharp crests, with no melted blobs. Replace the side-face lozenge row that reads as tyre tread with the ripples wrapping over the edge, or with a plain polished side face.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png, side.png and reverse.png show no vertical seam or break anywhere around the band. At 300 px the band reads as crisp wind-rippled sand, and the side faces no longer read as tread.

punch_list.zone: Tail (theta about 170 deg to -60 deg, riding beside the band's side face)
punch_list.change: Seat the tail on the shoulder of the crown, not beside the side face. Keep its outer edge within the band width, or at most 0.5 mm past it. Fuse its underside to the band along its whole length with a fillet of at least 0.4 mm. Keep the whorled cones.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and reverse.png the tail sits on the band and does not read as a separate spiked wire lying alongside it. In face.png the tail's outline stays inside the band edge.

punch_list.change: Update the section to the ring as built: lost wax, not Petrobond, and a sculpted 'Thorny devil' part with a sand-ripple band in place of the stamp rows, rosettes and flutes. Future reviewers can then check the author's claims against the right plan.
punch_list.acceptance: The section names lost wax and the sculpted part and lists the lost-wax gates.
